Overview

Steam Achievement Manager (SAM) is a portable desktop application for managing Steam achievements and statistics. The README documents a runtime dependency on the Steam client, a logged-in Steam account, and network access.

Core components

  • Steam API surface and client coordination — SAM.API/Client.cs
    Provides the API project’s client-facing coordination area, alongside SAM.API/Steam.cs, initialization failures, callbacks, and callback-related types.
  • Native Steam integration — SAM.API/NativeWrapper.cs
    Contains the native-wrapper boundary and supporting native classes/strings. Versioned interfaces under SAM.API/Interfaces and corresponding implementations under SAM.API/Wrappers represent Steam service contracts and alternative version-specific wrappers.
  • API callbacks and data types — SAM.API/Callbacks
    Defines callback implementations such as achievement/statistics-related notifications, with shared messages and result structures under SAM.API/Types. This is the event/data exchange area between Steam integration and application code.
  • Game management UI and domain model — SAM.Game/Manager.cs
    Owns the main game-management screen and its desktop interaction surface. Supporting achievement and statistic definitions, values, flags, and validation types are grouped under SAM.Game/Stats.
  • Game selection UI — SAM.Picker/GamePicker.cs
    Provides the separate game-picker screen and related game/logo presentation types, allowing the application to represent and select Steam games before management.

Entry points and public surface

SAM.Game/Program.cs and SAM.Picker/Program.cs are the two application startup areas indicated by the project layout. SAM.API/Steam.cs and SAM.API/Client.cs are the principal API-facing classes; consumers of the library-facing project can also work through its callback, interface, wrapper, and type areas.

Relationships

SAM.API owns communication with the external Steam client and exposes Steam-facing data/events. SAM.Game owns achievement/statistics management and its presentation model, while SAM.Picker owns game selection. The project organization indicates that the two application projects are separate consumers of the API area; the supplied evidence does not establish their exact import or call order.

External boundary

The Steam client, Steam account, and network are external actors and prerequisites, not repository components. The versioned interface/wrapper organization marks the principal integration boundary for Steam services. No repository-backed database or other persistent storage subsystem is identified by the supplied tree.
